clauses.statement: Every Graph writer that inserts, updates, or deletes a Graph entity row shares the Project identity transaction lock; multi-ID callers acquire deduplicated IDs in lexical order, lock contention fails immediately with a retryable 409, and unrelated IDs remain concurrent. Registered Project Catalog subjects reject generic entity-row writes and Graph Maintenance accepts only an exact active catalog projection. Edge-only writes reference endpoints but do not mutate those endpoint entity rows, so endpoint authorization and referential integrity remain separate guards.
clauses.rationale: A preflight-only lock cannot protect the canonical subject when another authenticated Graph writer can mutate the same global entity ID. A global coordinator would unnecessarily serialize unrelated projects and organizations, while waiting on per-ID locks acquired in different orders can deadlock; deterministic batch ordering plus fail-fast per-ID acquisition preserves safety and concurrency. Merely referencing an endpoint is not an entity-row mutation.

clauses.statement: A persisted project-provisioning-plan.v1 without graph_project_subject, or a run interrupted after its Graph materialization, receives a fresh bounded preflight before claim or write and resumes only when the current identity is absent, safely reusable, or proven by a fresh Graph receipt readback bound to that run's plan, apply receipt, target project, and idempotency key.
clauses.rationale: Adding a required plan field must not strand durable runs created before deployment, and a run must not reject the exact subject it already materialized before a later-step failure, while incompatible identities and external scopes must still fail before writes.
